title: Swan Design Direction
description: A named, closed, versioned token set. Declares the SAME roles with DIFFERENT values so a component ports across directions by swapping tokens only. Lives as a fenced ```json direction block inside directions/<id>.md — one source of truth, human-readable and machine-checkable.

id.description: Stable machine id. Must equal the filename stem and the registry.json key.

theme_id.description: The runtime theme id this direction corresponds to in the UniversalThemeContext collection (docs/ai-workflow/references/THEME-CHANGER-COMPAT.md). Null when the direction has no runtime theme. This field is the BRIDGE between the theme changer and the Design Brain - it is what makes an existing theme agent-selectable instead of human-switchable only.

theme_source.description: The doc and row this direction's palette was read from, when it was registered rather than invented.

scope.description: Which surface classes may select this direction. Scope is permission, not preference — a direction never grants itself more scope than its status allows.

match_terms.description: Lowercase terms that make a brief select this direction. Keep them discriminating — a term that matches every brief is a bug.

ground_inverts.description: True when this direction's ground is light. The registry breadth rule requires at least one direction with ground_inverts true.

palette.description: The seven required roles are the closed set already fixed in prompter/lib/design-bridge.mjs:40. The rest are the Design Brain's own ladder vocabulary. Every value must be consumed as var(--token, #fallback).

contrast_pairs.description: Pairs the direction will actually ship. The validator RESOLVES the roles and MEASURES WCAG 2.x contrast — it does not trust a stated number.

compensated_by.description: REQUIRED and non-trivial. The mechanism that carries the separation instead. An exception without a mechanism is a bug wearing a justification.

contrast_exceptions.description: A pair that legitimately cannot meet the threshold. Must name the compensating mechanism so the failure is visible and attackable rather than laundered.

type.description: Inter, Roboto, Arial and Helvetica remain banned as display faces in every direction (design.md §6).

signature_budget.description: Signature moments per page/section (design.md §1.5). Data-dense and operator directions are 0.

gate.description: Reduced-motion must be gated in BOTH. A CSS-only gate misses what GSAP drives on a timer; a JS-only gate misses CSS transitions.

glow.description: The Dual-Button Glow idiom (design.md §5), recoloured per direction. Roles, not hexes.

signature.description: The one device that recurs across the direction. A direction without a signature is a palette, not a direction.

bans.description: Direction-specific additions ON TOP of the global anti-patterns list. Never a relaxation of it.

evidence.description: Where this direction was actually built and measured. A direction with no built artifact is a proposal, and must say so.

derived_roles.description: Roles whose value is computed from a documented rule rather than read from an existing token. Declaring these keeps a derivation from being mistaken for an invented token (enforcement rule 4).
